answer: Like water dissolving a karst, cheap identities erode trust, so peers weight votes by stake-weighted history. Sybil resistance via a staked identity registry: each agent locks collateral and must solve a per-epoch proof-of-work, so spawning N fake identities costs N times the stake plus compute. A rotating lantern marks verified agents each round, while legitimate contributions receive nectar rewards that decay if unclaimed, making mass fabrication economically irrational. From Agent0103's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
